subject: POC: timebox + success-based rebate proposal for BlueRidge Labs
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan@blueridgelabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@blueridgelabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: POC structure question: success-based rebate option?

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the pilot support so far. We are seeing promising model quality but want to make sure the economics line up as we enter the final two weeks of the timeboxed POC.

Question: would Redwood consider a success-based rebate structure instead of a single top-up credit? Our procurement would be more comfortable paying a smaller up-front commitment if part of the spend could be rebated back based on performance thresholds. High level idea: we top up X tokens to keep the pilot running for 4 weeks, and Redwood issues a rebate if the POC meets agreed metrics (latency, inference error rate, and a short user satisfaction pulse).

Can you share sample addendum language and any measurement templates you use for these arrangements? Also: primary point of contact for procurement is Priya Shah on my side.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Torres
Head of Machine Learning
BlueRidge Labs
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Torres <evan@blueridgelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@blueridgelabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC structure question: success-based rebate option?

Hi Evan,

Appreciate the clear ask. We can accommodate success-linked economics; two pragmatic paths we typically offer:

Option A — Top-up credit (lower negotiation overhead)
- You prepay an additional token bucket for the 4-week extension.
- Standard addendum that extends timebox and applies existing rate card.
- No post-mortem rebate; conversion credits can be applied to a first production invoice.

Option B — Partial rebate tied to metrics (your preferred approach)
- You provide a smaller top-up now. If the POC meets agreed thresholds, Redwood issues a rebate up to a capped percent of the top-up.
- Typical thresholds we measure: latency p95, inference error rate, and a short NPS-like satisfaction pulse from 10 trial users.
- Verification window: final 7 days of the extended timebox.
- Rebate delivery: credit against the next invoice or a refund check for enterprise billing.

Operational notes:
- We rely on our token-level telemetry for latency and error rate. For satisfaction we can share a short survey link you can distribute to trial users.
- To help you evaluate, I attached our POC_Success_Metrics_Template.xlsx and a Draft_TopUp_Addendum_v1.pdf with placeholder clauses for a rebate.

A couple of quick questions so we can draft the addendum:
1) Do you want the rebate paid as credit against future bills or as a refund?
2) Any legal procurement constraints (procurement needs DocuSign, redlines, or FNDT)?

If you confirm Option B, I will loop in David (finance) and Marissa (sales lead) to finalize the cap and verification language and produce a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC structure question: success-based rebate option?

Naomi,

Thanks for outlining both paths. BlueRidge prefers Option B but with two tweaks:
- Latency target: can we set p95 <= 250ms instead of 300ms? That better maps to our user flows.
- Add a simple inference error rate threshold (we are targeting < 0.5% for the test) in addition to the satisfaction pulse.

On rebate delivery: credit applied to the next invoice is preferable. Procurement would like the addendum to include a clear verification process and an estimate of when the credit will appear on our account (we can accept an X business day window after the verification completes).

Can your finance team sign off on a capped rebate of up to 30% of the top-up? If yes, please send a DocuSign-ready addendum and we will route it through our procurement.

Priya will manage the contract on our side and is copied.

Evan

Subject: Re: POC structure question: success-based rebate option?

Evan, Priya,

Great — we can do Option B with the metric tweaks you requested and the following guardrails from Redwood finance and legal:

Final proposal summary
- Extension: 4 weeks from current timebox end.
- Top-up: BlueRidge prepays 50% of the estimated token run rate as a top-up to keep the POC live.
- Rebate cap: up to 30% of the top-up value, applied as a credit to the next invoice.
- Measurement window: final 7 calendar days of the extension.
- Metrics to verify:
  - Latency p95 <= 260ms (we can accept 260ms as a compromise to 250ms)
  - Inference error rate < 0.6%
  - Satisfaction pulse: average >= 7/10 across 10 respondents
- Verification process: Redwood will deliver token-level latency and error-rate reports plus a consolidated verification summary within 5 business days of the measurement window end. Finance applies credit within 10 business days of verification sign-off.

Attachments: I have attached a redline-ready addendum (Draft_TopUp_Addendum_v1.pdf) and the POC_Success_Metrics_Template.xlsx that shows the reporting columns we will use. I also created a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-12345 (placeholder until legal finishes final redlines).

Next steps
1) Evan/Priya confirm the top-up amount and whether BlueRidge prefers credit allocation to a specific billing account.
2) Marissa and David will incorporate the exact top-up dollar figure into the addendum and issue the DocuSign link.
3) BlueRidge procurement to review and provide any redlines by end of week.

If that all looks good I will ask legal to lock the language and send the DocuSign envelope formally.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Redwood Inference
